summary: Equity fell from 621.35 to 611.38 (-1.60%) on a day the SPY benchmark fell 1.96% and the shadow 1.52%. Since version 6 started (11-10) the account is -1.79%, against -3.23% for the shadow and -4.54% for SPY. The day's main event was the one the decision prepared for: SPY closed at 715.87, below the 730.02 line. The VOO and VTI stop blocks are now TRIPPED (-1.9%), on top of the RSP clause that had already tripped before the open. Together they are 23.25% of equity (13.27% + 9.98%) on one condition. The decision recorded the RSP trip in both theses and committed the Proposer to selling both. That was the right process call, since the PM cannot originate a sale. The cost is that the whole sleeve rode through a 2% index drop, roughly $2.9, because no sell proposal existed on the day the clause was already met. P1 (sell all of MCO) filled at 480.03 against the 481.29 mark. Its reasoning stands: it rests on the lost Financials premise, credit and beta, and drops the packet-artifact Industrials bucket the Skeptic objected to. MCO is buy-blocked until about 12-19. Rejecting P2 (the $15 WMT add) was also sound on the information at hand. The print-day gap could not be seen, XLP's 21-day clause had only 0.91 points of room, and the add would have reversed the 11-13 trim. WMT closed 126.04 (-0.97%), a modest reaction, so the Skeptic's 'reconsider if within 2-3% of 127.36' condition is now met. Avoiding a roughly $0.15 loss is not evidence either way. Staples cushioned the book but did not shelter it: WMT -0.97%, KR -1.61%, SAM -2.24%. Other stop blocks: EXEL is NEAR at 65.83 against $65 (+1.3%) after falling 3.6%, and INCY is 5.3% above its stop. Neither has tripped. FAST (-2.4%) is still the named next sell candidate on its met 'marginal hold' condition. Its price stop is 12.8% away. Problem for tomorrow: with SPY below the line, the code regime filter should now limit buys to BND, GLD, IEF and TLT. BND and IEF are wash-sale blocked, and the Market Analyst advises against gold and duration. Selling VOO and VTI would therefore push cash to about 38% with no buy available. That idle cash has a specific reason (the code filter plus tripped stops), not L4, and it should be stated as such rather than used to keep the ETFs.

broken_theses.why: Both invalidation clauses have now tripped. SPY closed 715.87, below the 730.02 200-day line (stop block TRIPPED, -1.9%), and RSP's 21-day return had already turned negative (-0.20%) before the open. Under the 11-17/11-18 pre-commitment and L9, the Proposer owes a full sale together with VTI at the next run, and the PM should approve it.

It shares VOO's stop and RSP clause, and both have tripped (SPY 715.87 vs 730.02; RSP 21d -0.20%). The $345.20 cost clause has not been hit (VTI is about $352). It is one position with VOO under L9 and should be sold in the same run.

lessons: A stored qualitative clause that has already tripped at decision time needs a sell proposal that same run. Recording it for the next run is not enough. On 11-19 the Market Analyst's note carried RSP 21d -0.20%, which met the VOO/VTI breadth clause, but neither the Proposer nor the Skeptic checked it. The PM caught it and could only write it into the theses, so 23% of the book stayed held through a 2% drop. The Proposer should check every stored clause numerically against the same-day Market Analyst figures before writing proposals (L7 applies to the Proposer too).

When a shared stop sits within about 0.5% of the line and the Market Analyst calls a close below it 'one ordinary session away', the decision should say plainly that the group will exit after a gap and at what likely cost. It should not treat holding as free. On 11-18 the PM rejected a half sale of VTI for a sound L9 reason, and that reasoning still holds. But the binary structure means the exit lands in full on the bad day, and that trade-off should be priced in the reasoning when the shared stop comes up again.

Not buying on a print day was right when the gap could not be seen and the position's own clause was close to tripping. Revisit the trade at the next run against the stated conditions, not today's P&L. WMT closed only 1% lower on the print, which meets the Skeptic's stated condition. Any WMT add still needs XLP 21d comfortably above +3% and a regime that allows stock buys.

Before a tripped shared stop forces a large sale under the regime filter, check which defensive buys are actually available. Tomorrow BND and IEF are wash-sale blocked and the Market Analyst advises against GLD and TLT, so the proceeds will sit in cash. Say in the reasoning that this cash is idle because of the code filter and the tripped theses, and do not use it as a reason to keep invalidated positions.
